subtopics.name: Types of Maps and Their Uses
objectives: Identify types of maps (topographical, atlas, sketch and statistical maps)
State the uses of maps in everyday life
Distinguish between maps, plans and globes

subtopics.name: Map Scales, Distances and Areas
objectives: Identify types of scale (statement, linear and representative fraction)
Convert between scale types and use scale to measure distances
Calculate areas of regular and irregular shapes on maps
Enlarge and reduce maps

subtopics.name: Map Reading and Interpretation
objectives: Interpret relief using contours, spot heights and trigonometric points
Identify landforms (ridges, spurs, valleys, plateaus) from contour patterns
Interpret drainage patterns and characteristics on topographical maps
Interpret settlement types, patterns and communication routes on maps
Draw and interpret cross profiles and determine intervisibility
Determine directions and bearings on maps

subtopics.name: Types of Statistical Maps and Diagrams
objectives: Identify statistical diagrams (bar graphs, line graphs, pie charts, divided rectangles)
Identify statistical maps (dot maps, choropleth, isopleth and flow maps)
State the advantages and disadvantages of each method

subtopics.name: Construction and Interpretation of Statistical Data
objectives: Construct bar graphs, line graphs and pie charts from geographical data
Interpret statistical maps and diagrams
Compute percentages, averages, densities and ratios from geographic data

subtopics.name: Chain and Prismatic Surveying
objectives: State the purposes and instruments of chain and prismatic surveying
Describe the procedures and stages of chain and prismatic surveys
Identify problems associated with each survey type and produce simple survey plans

subtopics.name: Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
objectives: Define GIS and identify its components (hardware, software, data, people, methods)
Identify sources of geographic data (maps, remote sensing, GPS, fieldwork)
State the uses of GIS in mapping, planning and resource management
Identify problems of GIS application in Nigeria

subtopics.name: The Earth in the Solar System
objectives: Describe the position of the earth in the solar system
Describe the shape and size of the earth with proofs of its sphericity
Explain earth rotation and revolution and their effects (day/night, seasons)

subtopics.name: Latitude, Longitude and Time
objectives: Distinguish between latitude and longitude and identify important lines
Calculate distances using lines of latitude
Calculate local time and time zones using lines of longitude
Explain the International Date Line and Greenwich Mean Time

subtopics.name: Structure of the Earth
objectives: Describe the internal structure of the earth (crust, mantle, core)
Describe the external spheres of the earth (atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, lithosphere)

subtopics.name: Types and Characteristics of Rocks
objectives: Classify rocks into igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic types
Describe the characteristics and modes of formation of each rock type
Give examples of each rock type

subtopics.name: Importance and Uses of Rocks
objectives: State the uses of rocks to man (minerals, construction, soil formation)
Explain the process of rock weathering and the rock cycle

subtopics.name: Internal (Endogenetic) Processes and Landforms
objectives: Explain earth movements: folding, faulting, vulcanicity and earthquakes
Identify landforms produced by internal processes (fold mountains, block mountains, rift valleys, volcanoes)
Describe the distribution and effects of earthquakes and volcanoes

subtopics.name: External (Exogenetic) Processes: Weathering and Mass Movement
objectives: Distinguish between physical, chemical and biological weathering
Explain factors affecting weathering and types of mass movement
Describe karst (limestone) landforms and their features

subtopics.name: Landforms of Water, Wind and Ice Action
objectives: Describe erosional and depositional landforms of rivers (valleys, waterfalls, deltas, floodplains)
Describe coastal landforms of wave action (cliffs, beaches, spits, bars)
Describe desert landforms of wind action (barchans, seifs, zeugens, yardangs)
Describe glacial landforms (corries, aretes, U-valleys, moraines)

subtopics.name: Oceans and Seas
objectives: Identify the major oceans and seas of the world
Explain the characteristics of ocean water: salinity and temperature
Explain ocean currents, their causes, types and effects on coastal regions
Explain tides and waves and their importance

subtopics.name: Rivers, Lakes and Underground Water
objectives: Describe river systems, drainage patterns and river regimes
Classify lakes by origin and state their importance
Explain sources and features of underground water (springs, wells, aquifers)

subtopics.name: Elements of Weather and Climate and Their Measurement
objectives: Distinguish between weather and climate
Identify the elements of weather (temperature, rainfall, pressure, wind, humidity, sunshine, cloud cover)
Describe weather instruments and their uses
Explain types of rainfall (convectional, orographic/relief, cyclonic/frontal)

subtopics.name: Factors Affecting Climate
objectives: Explain the factors affecting temperature and climate (latitude, altitude, continentality, ocean currents, winds)
Explain pressure belts and planetary wind systems
Explain local winds (harmattan, land and sea breezes)

subtopics.name: Classification and Types of Climate
objectives: Classify climates using the Greek and Koppen systems
Describe the characteristics and distribution of major climate types (equatorial, tropical continental, desert, Mediterranean, temperate, tundra)
Relate climate types to human activities

subtopics.name: Types and Distribution of World Vegetation
objectives: Identify major vegetation zones: forests (tropical rainforest, temperate, coniferous), grasslands (savanna, temperate grassland) and deserts
Describe the characteristics of each vegetation zone
Relate vegetation zones to climate

subtopics.name: Importance and Human Impact on Vegetation
objectives: State the importance of vegetation to man
Explain the impact of human activities on natural vegetation (deforestation, bush burning, overgrazing)

subtopics.name: Soil Formation, Profile and Types
objectives: Define soil and explain the factors and processes of soil formation
Describe the soil profile and soil constituents
Classify soils (zonal, azonal, intrazonal) and describe tropical soil types

subtopics.name: Soil Importance, Problems and Conservation
objectives: State the importance of soil to man
Explain causes and effects of soil erosion and soil degradation
Describe methods of soil conservation

subtopics.name: Types of Environmental Resources
objectives: Identify types of environmental resources (atmospheric, land, soil, vegetation, mineral and water resources)
Distinguish between renewable and non-renewable resources
Give examples and uses of each resource type

subtopics.name: Resource Conservation and Management
objectives: Explain the concept and need for resource conservation
Describe methods of conserving environmental resources

subtopics.name: Ecosystems and Environmental Balance
objectives: Define ecosystem and describe the components of land ecosystems
Explain the interrelationships within an ecosystem (food chain, food web, energy flow)
Explain how human activities affect environmental balance

subtopics.name: Environmental Hazards and Their Management
objectives: Identify natural hazards (drought, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, flooding) and their effects
Identify man-induced hazards (deforestation, desertification, soil erosion, pollution, flooding)
Explain the causes, effects, prevention and control of environmental hazards
Explain global environmental issues (global warming, climate change, ozone layer depletion)

subtopics.name: World Population: Distribution, Growth and Structure
objectives: Explain the concepts of population distribution, density and growth
Identify factors affecting population distribution
Describe population structure (age and sex composition, population pyramids)
Explain factors of population change (birth rate, death rate, migration)

subtopics.name: Migration and Population Problems
objectives: Explain types, causes and effects of migration (rural-urban, international)
Explain problems of rapid population growth (overpopulation) and underpopulation
Describe population policies and census

subtopics.name: Types and Patterns of Settlement
objectives: Distinguish between rural and urban settlements
Identify settlement patterns (nucleated, dispersed, linear) and factors affecting them
Explain the functions of rural and urban settlements

subtopics.name: Urbanization and Settlement Interaction
objectives: Explain urbanization, its causes and problems in developing countries
Explain the interrelationships between rural and urban settlements
Describe the hierarchy of settlements and spheres of influence

subtopics.name: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Activities
objectives: Classify economic activities into primary, secondary and tertiary types
Describe types of agriculture (subsistence, commercial, plantation, pastoral) and factors affecting agriculture
Describe mining, lumbering, fishing and their importance
Explain manufacturing industries: types, location factors and importance

subtopics.name: Transportation, Communication and Trade
objectives: Identify modes of transportation (road, rail, water, air, pipeline) with their advantages and disadvantages
Explain the importance of transportation and communication to economic development
Explain world trade: factors, patterns and major trading blocs

subtopics.name: Location, Size and Political Divisions
objectives: Describe the location, position and size of Nigeria
Identify Nigeria's states, capitals and neighbouring countries
Explain the importance of Nigeria's location in Africa

subtopics.name: Relief, Drainage, Climate and Vegetation of Nigeria
objectives: Describe the relief regions (highlands and lowlands) of Nigeria
Describe the drainage systems: rivers Niger and Benue and their tributaries, Lake Chad
Describe the climatic zones and seasons of Nigeria
Describe the vegetation belts of Nigeria (mangrove, rainforest, guinea, sudan and sahel savanna) and their characteristics

topics.name: Nigeria: Population, Resources and Economic Activities

subtopics.name: Population and Settlement in Nigeria
objectives: Describe the distribution and density of Nigeria's population
Explain migration patterns and urbanization in Nigeria
Identify major urban centres and their functions

subtopics.name: Agriculture and Mineral Resources of Nigeria
objectives: Identify Nigeria's major food and cash crops and their producing areas
Explain the problems and importance of agriculture in Nigeria
Identify Nigeria's mineral resources (petroleum, gas, coal, tin, iron ore, limestone) and their locations
Explain the importance of petroleum to the Nigerian economy

subtopics.name: Industry, Transport and Trade in Nigeria
objectives: Identify major manufacturing industries and industrial zones in Nigeria
Describe transportation networks in Nigeria and their problems
Describe Nigeria's internal and external trade

subtopics.name: Environmental Problems in Nigeria
objectives: Identify environmental problems in Nigeria (soil erosion, desertification, flooding, oil pollution, deforestation)
Explain the causes, effects and solutions to these environmental problems by region

subtopics.name: ECOWAS and Regional Cooperation
objectives: State the origin, aims and member countries of ECOWAS
Explain the benefits and problems of ECOWAS
Explain Nigeria's role in regional and international cooperation
